- **091304 zip**: 17 js files = the same set + js/common/reviewVerdicts.js, and its code requires it → self-consistent too!

So BOTH zips are internally self-consistent. The runtime failure (`Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`) happened because fa's installer had **already installed `sm_github-0.1.36`** (the 075526 content, or a mix) into `/home/runner/.dmtools/packs/sm_github-0.1.36/` and **did not re-install when the "new" 0.1.36 appeared** — the version number was unchanged, so the cache stayed. But wait — if the cache held the OLD (075526) content, the old code doesn't require reviewVerdicts → no failure...

Hmm, unless the installer DOES re-extract when the release tag changes (it keys the cache by version dir but re-extracts on a changed artifact? or it verifies sha256?). If it re-extracts the 091304 zip over the 075526 directory... the 091304 zip is a superset — that would produce a complete new tree (the zip contains all files, overwrite everything). That works fine too.

The mixed state must come from a DIFFERENT mechanism: maybe fa resolves `@latest` → release 091304 → downloads `sm_github-0.1.36.zip`... and compares against the installed version 0.1.36 → SKIPS download → runs OLD code... → no failure. Still not matching.

If dmtools resolves relative requires from the js/ ROOT (not the file's own dir), then `js/common/smProvider.js`'s `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')` → `js/reviewVerdicts.js` → MISSING in both zips!! But then the 075526-era... no, 075526 has no such require at all.

Hmm wait, but if dmtools resolved relative requires from the js/ root, then `js/common/smProvider.js` requiring `./ticketKeyShapes.js` would need `js/ticketKeyShapes.js` — and packs ship js/common/ticketKeyShapes.js... that would have failed forever. So dmtools must resolve relative to the requiring file (Node-style). Then `./reviewVerdicts.js` from js/common/smProvider.js = js/common/reviewVerdicts.js — present in 091304 zip.

So the failing runtime had NEW smProvider.js but NO js/common/reviewVerdicts.js on disk. The mixed state: the installer updated SOME files but not others? OR — the fa runner at 09:36 was running a pack directory populated from the 091304 zip where the installer... hmm.

The 091304 release published `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` with different content (sha256 2035... vs 0dc6...) than the 075526 release's `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` — **two releases, same version string, different bytes**. This violates AC2 directly, and is what allowed a consumer that had 075526's 0.1.36 cached/installed to end up running mixed/stale content when the "new 0.1.36" appeared (installer skips or partially refreshes when the version is unchanged — dmtools-dart behavior, but the PIPELINE handed it two different artifacts under one version key).

That tolerance is the root cause. Also note: a release whose ledger push failed is INVISIBLE in versions.json — the ledger claims 0.1.35 while 0.1.36 packs are live. The next content change bumps 0.1.35→0.1.36 AGAIN → guaranteed collision.

### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

Exports:

- `resolveRequire(fromPath, spec)` — resolve spec relative to fromPath's dir, normalize (no leading './', collapse '../'), returns zip-style path. If spec doesn't end with '.js', append '.js' (dmtools require convention in this repo always uses .js).
- `unresolvedRequires(files)` — files: array of {path, source}. Returns array of {from, spec, target} where target not in the set of file paths. Pure — no zip needed; the caller extracts zip contents.
- `missingFromZip(entries, jsPaths)` — hmm, simpler: caller unzips the pack to temp, walks `.js` files, reads sources, builds path set, calls unresolvedRequires. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.

### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.
"}

### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.
"}

Also I realize the other test "unresolved requires FAIL the release (throw → non-zero step)" has a sloppy assertion:

```js
assert.ok(/assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s/.test(builder) ||
    builder.indexOf('function assertZipRequires(') !== -1, ...);
```

The regex `assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s` — non-greedy match from any assertZipRequires( to the first `{` followed by throw — `\s*\{` requires `{` IMMEDIATELY after whitespace following the (…) — `[\s\S]*?` could span far. Actually `assertZipRequires\(` then `[\s\S]*?` (anything) then `\{\s*throw\s` — it looks for any `{throw` after an assertZipRequires( occurrence. In my builder, the definition is `function assertZipRequires(zipPath) {\n  const tmp...` — no throw directly. But the throw inside is `throw new Error(...)` after `if (unresolved.length > 0) {`. The regex with [\s\S]*? would find: first `assertZipRequires(` occurrence → then lazily expand to the first `{` followed by whitespace+throw... `if (unresolved.length > 0) {\n      throw new Error` — the `{` followed by `\n      throw` matches `\{\s*throw\s`? `\{\s*throw\s` — `{`, whitespace*, `throw`, whitespace — yes matches. So the regex passes as long as SOME assertZipRequires( is followed somewhere by {throw. Sloppy but functionally asserts "gate + throw coexist". Let me tighten it: find the definition block and check it contains throw:

```js
var defStart = builder.indexOf('function assertZipRequires(');
var defEnd = builder.indexOf('\n}', defStart);  // hmm fragile
```

Better: slice from defStart to the next top-level function or use a bounded slice: `builder.slice(defStart, defStart + 2500).indexOf('throw new Error')`. That's a genuine containment assertion. Let me rewrite that test cleanly.

messages.preview: The plot thickens — **eight consecutive releases** (all of Oct 8 + Oct 9 morning) already reused `sm_github: 0.1.36`. And PR #810's squash *added* versions.json (69 new lines). Let me check what the e…

blocks.text:
MAJOR finding! 

1. **PR #810's squash commit ADDED versions.json from scratch** (`69 +` lines, new file — `181722 insertions(+)` across 940 files?! That looks like the whole repo was (re)added — the branch history is weird, maybe the repo was re-initialized. Actually 940 files with 181k insertions in a "bug fix" PR is bizarre... wait, that's the diff vs its parent. Hmm, actually maybe the PR branch had a broken merge and the squash effectively re-created files. OR the repo history was rewritten. Whatever — the key fact: e0a2da7 is versions.json's ONLY commit; before it, versions.json did NOT exist on main! The ledger was never on main before 09:11 on Oct 9. All releases before that ran with... wait, the builder REQUIRES versions.json (readVersions). If main had no versions.json, every release run would crash... unless the runs' checkouts had versions.json from... hmm.

Hold on — actually maybe the repo was re-created/migrated (the `181722 insertions` across 940 files = whole tree added). Let me check e0a2da7's parent... `e0a2da7^` gave "bad revision" — because in a shallow clone? Let me check `git rev-parse e0a2da7^` / whether this is a shallow checkout (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`). The clone might be shallow (fetch-depth 1) — but then `git tag --list` showed the tag and `git diff BASE_REF...HEAD` logic... Let me check.

2. **The version collision is SYSTEMIC**: catalogs from ALL of Oct 8's five releases + Oct 9's 071349 already advertise sm_github=**0.1.36** — BEFORE the incident pair! So sm_github-0.1.36.zip was published in at least 7 releases (Oct8 ×5, 071349, 075526, 091304) — the version number 0.1.36 has been REUSED across many releases with (presumably) different contents all along. The ledger never landed on main between releases, so every release recomputed from the same stale base version → same numbers republished all day.

So the ACTUAL root cause of "same version, different content" is now crystal clear and much bigger than one bad release:

**The version ledger (versions.json) never lands on main.** Evidence:
- versions.json did not exist on main until e0a2da7 (2026-10-09 12:11 +0300 = 09:11 UTC, the #810 squash — which carried the ledger as part of its tree).

### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.
"}

Also I realize the other test "unresolved requires FAIL the release (throw → non-zero step)" has a sloppy assertion:

```js
assert.ok(/assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s/.test(builder) ||
    builder.indexOf('function assertZipRequires(') !== -1, ...);
```

The regex `assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s` — non-greedy match from any assertZipRequires( to the first `{` followed by throw — `\s*\{` requires `{` IMMEDIATELY after whitespace following the (…) — `[\s\S]*?` could span far. Actually `assertZipRequires\(` then `[\s\S]*?` (anything) then `\{\s*throw\s` — it looks for any `{throw` after an assertZipRequires( occurrence. In my builder, the definition is `function assertZipRequires(zipPath) {\n  const tmp...` — no throw directly. But the throw inside is `throw new Error(...)` after `if (unresolved.length > 0) {`. The regex with [\s\S]*? would find: first `assertZipRequires(` occurrence → then lazily expand to the first `{` followed by whitespace+throw... `if (unresolved.length > 0) {\n      throw new Error` — the `{` followed by `\n      throw` matches `\{\s*throw\s`? `\{\s*throw\s` — `{`, whitespace*, `throw`, whitespace — yes matches. So the regex passes as long as SOME assertZipRequires( is followed somewhere by {throw. Sloppy but functionally asserts "gate + throw coexist". Actually — hold on. Maybe versions.json DID exist on main, and #810 CHANGED it (69 lines could be modifications in a 69-line file — "69 +" with no "-" means pure additions; for a full rewrite it'd show 69+/69-). Pure 69 additions = NEW file (the file has 69 lines ≈ my cat showed ~69 lines). So #810 added versions.json to main.

So where did #810's BRANCH get versions.json (sm_github 0.1.35)? The branch merged origin/main mid-flight (mentioned in the commit message: "The merge of origin/main (gh-806 #811) into ai/gh-807")... that implies main HAD versions.json via #811?? But then the squash wouldn't "add" it...

UNLESS the shallow clone's diff is vs a FAKE parent... whatever. The shallow clone limits archaeology. What's PROVABLE:

1. **Catalogs prove version reuse**: sm_github was labeled 0.1.36 in every release from Oct 8 09:55 through Oct 9 09:13 (8 releases), while its content changed (at minimum between 075526 and 091304 — proven by sha256). Whatever the ledger's exact journey, the pipeline PUBLISHED the same version for different content, repeatedly.

2. **The tag 091304 carries versions.json with sm_github=0.1.35** while its own catalog advertises 0.1.36 — the ledger at release time did not reflect what was being published. (Builder bumped in-memory to 0.1.36, published, and the ledger push to main either failed or landed inside #810's squash at 09:11 — either way, the 091304 run started from a ledger saying 0.1.35, same as 075526 did.)

3. So the mechanism for the collision is confirmed: **both the 075526 run and the 091304 run started from the same stale ledger state (sm_github=0.1.35), both computed next=0.1.36, both published `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` with different content** (075526 = pre-#810 tree, 091304 = post-#810 tree). The registry/catalog then pointed consumers at 0.1.36 → consumers that had installed the 075526 0.1.36 saw "already installed, same version" and either kept running the old mixed state or partially refreshed — the exact failure mode the ticket describes (require of a file the installed copy lacked).

And the secondary wrinkle I found: the ticket's claim "the 091304 pack is missing reviewVerdicts.js" is **not** what the artifacts show — the 091304 zip contains the file. The breakage is the version collision + consumer caching, i.e., exactly what the Goal/AC2 targets: "every release that changes pack content bumps the pack version". (I'll note this RCA refinement in rca.md and response.md.)

Wait, one more check on the "half-installed" state: the mitigation pinned registry to 075526 — pinned the RELEASE TAG base URL. After pinning, fa re-resolved... the 075526 release... whose catalog ALSO says 0.1.36 → installer: installed version == 0.1.36 → skip?? But mitigation WORKED (ticks green). So the installer must key its cache by (release tag, version) or by artifact sha256... or the pin changes the base URL so it re-downloads and re-extracts regardless of version. Since pinning to the old tag FIXED it while both tags say 0.1.36, the installer must re-extract when the release tag changes → after unpin (back to latest), the tick would fetch 091304's zip (0.1.36, complete content) → should ALSO work... unless the installer skips when version matches the cached one (0.1.36 cached from... hmm).

Whatever the precise installer policy (non-goal, dmtools-dart), the pipeline-level defect stands: **the release pipeline republishes changed content under an unchanged version**, which no consumer-caching scheme can disambiguate.

NOW — the FIX, mapped to the capability surface + ACs:

**Fix 1 (AC2 — version uniqueness, the root cause):** In `ci/release_packs.mjs`, guarantee "same version ⇒ same content": for every agent NOT bumped by the affected set (built at its unchanged `current` version), compare the freshly built zip's sha256 against the same-named asset in the PREVIOUS release (base ref tag). If the content differs → the version is stale → bump it (and rebuild). This makes "two releases with differing pack content" never share a version string. Implementation details:

- Simpler, self-contained alternative that doesn't need network: **build first at the current version, hash it; if it equals what... ** no — without the previous artifact there's nothing to compare against locally. BUT the builder CAN fetch the previous release via `gh release download` (gh is available in the workflow, GH_TOKEN set in publish step; the build step doesn't currently have GH_TOKEN — need to add env).
- Even simpler and fully offline: **content-address the version bump decision by the SOURCE tree**: hash the inputs that go into the pack (the entry config + js/ + instructions/ + prompts/... i.e., everything compile includes). If the hash differs from the hash recorded for the current version... but we don't have the old hash recorded anywhere reliable (that's the whole problem — the ledger lies).

  Hmm. But wait: we could make the ledger honest by committing a content-hash map ALONGSIDE the version bump — but the failure was precisely that ledger pushes don't land...

  OK here's the thing though — why don't ledger pushes land? "direct ledger push rejected — main moved; the next release recomputes versions from main" — with strict main protection, a direct push of the ledger would be rejected EVERY time (rulesets!). The comment says "the ai-teammate app holds a ruleset bypass on main-protection" — but the release workflow pushes with `secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` — GITHUB_TOKEN of the release run has NO bypass. So if SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN is unset/without bypass, the ledger push fails EVERY run → the ledger on main NEVER updates via releases → every release recomputes the same stale base → systemic version reuse (exactly what the catalogs show!). The versions.json that exists on main NOW (0.1.35/0.1.34...) came from #810's branch — the agent's branch had it? Weird but whatever.

  So a ROBUST fix can't depend on the ledger being current on main — it must derive uniqueness from the RELEASE HISTORY itself (GitHub releases are append-only and can't be rewritten by a failed push): i.e., **compare against the previous release's artifacts**. ### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.
"}

(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.
"}

assert.ok(/assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s/.test(builder) ||

The regex `assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s` — non-greedy match from any assertZipRequires( to the first `{` followed by throw — `\s*\{` requires `{` IMMEDIATELY after whitespace following the (…) — `[\s\S]*?` could span far. Actually `assertZipRequires\(` then `[\s\S]*?` (anything) then `\{\s*throw\s` — it looks for any `{throw` after an assertZipRequires( occurrence. In my builder, the definition is `function assertZipRequires(zipPath) {\n  const tmp...` — no throw directly. But the throw inside is `throw new Error(...)` after `if (unresolved.length > 0) {`. The regex with [\s\S]*? would find: first `assertZipRequires(` occurrence → then lazily expand to the first `{` followed by whitespace+throw... `if (unresolved.length > 0) {\n      throw new Error` — the `{` followed by `\n      throw` matches `\{\s*throw\s`? `\{\s*throw\s` — `{`, whitespace*, `throw`, whitespace — yes matches. So the regex passes as long as SOME assertZipRequires( is followed somewhere by {throw. Sloppy but functionally asserts "gate + throw coexist". blocks.text:
### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`

I have enough context. Now let me write the RCA first (as required: outputs/rca.md FIRST), then implement following TDD:

1. **RED**: Write failing reproduction tests first:
   - `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` doesn't exist yet → tests fail.

2. **GREEN**: Implement `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` + `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs`, wire into `ci/release_packs.mjs` + workflow, document rollback contract in docs/machine-factory-integration.md.
3. Run tests via dmtools runner.

Let me first verify how tests run: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_releasePacks.json`. Let me run the EXISTING suite first to confirm green baseline.

Then design the implementation concretely:

### New module: `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (CommonJS, GraalJS-safe: var, no arrows, no template literals)

Exports:
- `requireSpecs(source)` — extract string-literal relative require specs from JS source: regex `/\brequire\s*\(\s*(['"])(\.\.?\/[^'"]*)\1\s*\)/g`. Returns array of specs.
- `resolveRequire(fromPath, spec)` — resolve spec relative to fromPath's dir, normalize (no leading './', collapse '../'), returns zip-style path. If spec doesn't end with '.js', append '.js' (dmtools require convention in this repo always uses .js).
- `unresolvedRequires(files)` — files: array of {path, source}. Returns array of {from, spec, target} where target not in the set of file paths. Pure — no zip needed; the caller extracts zip contents.
- `missingFromZip(entries, jsPaths)` — hmm, simpler: caller unzips the pack to temp, walks `.js` files, reads sources, builds path set, calls unresolvedRequires. Also verify... the gate function used by release_packs: `checkPackZip(zipPath)` — but that needs node fs + zip exec — keep THAT wiring in release_packs.mjs (ESM, node-only), gate module stays pure (testable in GraalJS). 

### New module: `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (CommonJS, GraalJS-safe)

Exports:
- `payloadFingerprint(manifestJson)` — parse manifest JSON string → normalize `(path, sha256)` pairs sorted → string. Ignore non-`files` metadata (source commit etc.). Actually: manifest.files = [{path, sha256, mode?}]. Sort by path, join `path:sha256`. Return string.
- `fingerprintsDiffer(prevManifestJson, nextManifestJson)` → boolean.
- `resolveBumps(...)` — decision helper: given `{agent → {currentVersion, affected, prevManifestJson, nextManifestJson}}`... hmm, keep it minimal: `contentChanged = fingerprintsDiffer(prev, next)`. The bump loop lives in release_packs.mjs.

Wait — do I need the manifest BEFORE the version is final? Chicken-and-egg: build produces `<agent>-<version>.zip` with the version stamped inside the manifest? Does the manifest contain the version? Let me check the manifest of the pack I built: /tmp/packtest/manifest.json. If the manifest contains the version field, then fingerprinting the whole manifest is version-sensitive → always "differs" → always bump. That's why I restrict the fingerprint to the `files` array (path+sha256) — payload only. Let me check the manifest fields.

Also the zip file NAME contains the version — rebuilding at a bumped version = recompile (buildPack) + augment again. Fine.

Flow in main() per agent (non-dry):
```
var next = affected.includes(agent) ? bump(current, BUMP) : current;
var zip = buildPack(agent, next); augmentLaunchSurface(agent, zip);
if (!affected.includes(agent) && prevManifestJson) {
    if (fingerprintsDiffer(prevManifestJson, readManifestFromZip(zip))) {
        next = bump(next, BUMP);  // second bump: 0.1.36 → 0.1.37
        zip = buildPack(agent, next); augmentLaunchSurface(agent, zip);
    }
gate: checkPackRequires(zip) → throws on unresolved
validatePack(zip)
versions[agent] = next;
```

prevManifestJson source: downloaded previous release asset `<agent>-<current>.zip` → extract manifest.json. Downloading EVERY unbumped agent's zip every release = ~60 small downloads... acceptable? Each pack zip is ~100KB-1MB? sm_github zip is what size? Let me check. 60 downloads × ~200KB = 12MB per release — fine for CI. But it doubles release time (downloads serial). Could parallelize... keep simple, serial; note in response.

Alternative cheaper: download only the CATALOG from previous release + compare... no, catalog has only version numbers — the collision problem is precisely that versions match while content differs; must compare CONTENT. OK, download.

But ALSO: the base VERSION should come from the previous catalog when the ledger is stale! Both 075526 and 091304 read 0.1.35 from the (stale/absent) ledger and bumped to 0.1.36. If instead the builder reads the PREVIOUS RELEASE's catalog.json (sm_github=0.1.36 as shipped), then: base=0.1.36 → bump → 0.1.37. The compare-and-bump then wouldn't even be needed for THIS case... but the ledger is still the fallback. Do BOTH:
- `--prev-release-tag <tag>`: builder downloads catalog.json from the tag (one small file) → `shippedVersions` = catalog content; base version for every agent = shippedVersions[agent] || versions[agent] || '0.1.0'. This alone fixes the systemic version reuse (versions always move past what's actually published).
- Content compare-and-bump as the safety net for the unbumped agents (protects against any residual staleness: e.g., catalog download failed → fallback to versions.json which may be stale → unbumped agent rebuilt with changed content at same version → compare catches it → bump).

Hmm wait — if the catalog download fails (no gh/network), the content compare ALSO can't download the prev zips. Then we're back today's behavior (degrade + warn). Acceptable: primary environment (release workflow) has gh.

Manual dispatches: `steps.base.outputs.ref` is computed for dispatch runs too (Compute base ref step always runs). So `--prev-release-tag` gets passed always. Dry-run: no downloads? Downloading in dry-run is harmless but needs gh + token; dry-run is used to preview. Let me make downloads best-effort with clear warnings (never fail the build when the PREV data is unavailable — but the require GATE and validate DO fail the build; that's the point).

Wait, careful about ONE thing: when compare-and-bump triggers (agent not in affected set but content differs), the version moves TWO patches ahead of the stale ledger (0.1.35 → 0.1.36 → 0.1.37)? No — with catalog-derived base (0.1.36 shipped), unbumped agent stays 0.1.36; content compare: built zip vs shipped 0.1.36 zip → differs (post-#810 content vs pre) → bump → 0.1.37. Good: 091304 would have shipped sm_github-0.1.37.zip. And fa's cache (0.1.36) would refresh. AC4: tick resolves all requires on the fixed release.

### Require-gate wiring (release_packs.mjs)

After augmentLaunchSurface + before/after validatePack:
```
assertPackRequires(zipPath)  // unzip to temp, walk *.js, resolve relative requires, throw listing unresolved
```
Implementation in release_packs.mjs (node): execSync unzip -o to mkdtemp, readdirSync recursive, read each .js, build Set of paths, use gate module's unresolvedRequires(files, paths) → if non-empty throw Error with details. Temp cleanup in finally.

Note: augmentLaunchSurface already unzips for teammate packs but doesn't keep the tmp dir. I'll do a standalone gate pass — simple and pack-type agnostic.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The pack-release pipeline republished changed pack content under an unchanged version string — `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` shipped twice with different bytes (`agents-rel-20261009-075526` sha256 `0dc62ca4…`, `agents-rel-20261009-091304` sha256 `20352463…`, both catalogs advertising `sm_github: 0.1.36`) — and version-keyed consumers (fa installer cache at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/`) then ran mixed content: post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` against an installed 0.1.36 tree that lacked it → every `machine-sm` tick failed with `Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js`.

**Root cause**: two compounding pipeline defects in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` + `ci/release_packs.mjs`:

1. **Version numbers are derived from a ledger that does not reflect what was actually shipped.** `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads the base version from `versions.json` on main and bumps locally. The ledger push back to main is best-effort (a rejected direct push only warns: "the next release recomputes versions from main"), so it never landed: `versions.json` was absent from main until the #810 squash (09:11Z) and still said `sm_github: 0.1.35` at the 091304 tag. Evidence: the catalogs of EIGHT consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertise `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed underneath. Both the 075526 and 091304 runs therefore computed `0.1.35 → 0.1.36` from the same stale base and published different zips under the same name. Nothing in the pipeline ever compares the freshly built artifact against what the same version already shipped.
2. **No release sanity gate on pack self-consistency.** `validatePack()` (ci/release_packs.mjs) only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves; it never checks that every `require('./x')` in the packed JS resolves to a file inside the zip. A pack whose code requires a missing file (whatever the packing CLI's closure logic did that morning — the pinned dmtools release at incident time was older than today's 0.1.43, which does include the file) sails through validation, publication and cataloguing, and is only caught live by red fa ticks.

**Impact**: any consumer resolving `@latest`/`@<version>` can silently run stale or mixed pack content after every ledger-push failure (which, given main's ruleset, is effectively every release). Worst case observed: ~25 min of fully red SM ticks, manual mitigation pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to the 075526 tag.

**Correction to the ticket narrative (verified against the artifacts)**: the 091304 zip is NOT missing `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — it contains the file (17 js files) and is internally self-consistent. The 075526 zip (16 js files) also is. The breakage is purely the version collision: the installer had 0.1.36 on disk, the registry then advertised a *different* 0.1.36, and the version-keyed cache produced a tree with new requiring code but no new file. The fix therefore targets version uniqueness (AC2), not zip file inclusion — though the missing-file gate (AC3) is still built as demanded, red-team-tested against the mixed-content shape.

**Fix approach** (all in this repo; dmtools-dart installer caching stays a non-goal):

1. `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): payload fingerprint from the manifest `files` array (path+sha256, ignoring `version`/`sourceCommit` metadata), plus version-resolution helpers: base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (the release history is append-only and cannot lie, unlike the ledger) over `versions.json`; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` (downloads previous release `catalog.json` + same-version zips via `gh`, best-effort with warnings) — replaying the incident, 091304 would have shipped `sm_github-0.1.37.zip`.
2. `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new, pure, GraalJS-testable): extracts literal relative `require('./…')`/`require('../…')` specs from every `.js` in a built zip (including lazy requires nested in function bodies), resolves them against the zip's file set, and fails the release (`throw` → non-zero step) listing unresolved targets. Wired into `ci/release_packs.mjs` after the launch-surface augment, before validate/publish (AC1, AC3).
3. Rollback contract documented in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` (pinning `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the mitigation used live).
4. Unit tests: gate + guard modules (L1), incident-shape fixtures that the gate must FAIL (L2 red-team), builder/workflow wiring assertions extending `js/unit-tests/test_releasePacks.js`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-812.

blocks.text:
Also I realize the other test "unresolved requires FAIL the release (throw → non-zero step)" has a sloppy assertion:

```js
assert.ok(/assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s/.test(builder) ||
    builder.indexOf('function assertZipRequires(') !== -1, ...);
```

The regex `assertZipRequires\([\s\S]*?\{\s*throw\s` — non-greedy match from any assertZipRequires( to the first `{` followed by throw — `\s*\{` requires `{` IMMEDIATELY after whitespace following the (…) — `[\s\S]*?` could span far. Actually `assertZipRequires\(` then `[\s\S]*?` (anything) then `\{\s*throw\s` — it looks for any `{throw` after an assertZipRequires( occurrence. In my builder, the definition is `function assertZipRequires(zipPath) {\n  const tmp...` — no throw directly. But the throw inside is `throw new Error(...)` after `if (unresolved.length > 0) {`. The regex with [\s\S]*? would find: first `assertZipRequires(` occurrence → then lazily expand to the first `{` followed by whitespace+throw... `if (unresolved.length > 0) {\n      throw new Error` — the `{` followed by `\n      throw` matches `\{\s*throw\s`? `\{\s*throw\s` — `{`, whitespace*, `throw`, whitespace — yes matches. So the regex passes as long as SOME assertZipRequires( is followed somewhere by {throw. Sloppy but functionally asserts "gate + throw coexist". Let me tighten it: find the definition block and check it contains throw:

```js
var defStart = builder.indexOf('function assertZipRequires(');
var defEnd = builder.indexOf('\n}', defStart);  // hmm fragile
```

Better: slice from defStart to the next top-level function or use a bounded slice: `builder.slice(defStart, defStart + 2500).indexOf('throw new Error')`. That's a genuine containment assertion. Let me rewrite that test cleanly.

### Pack launch surface (Wave 2 — self-sufficient teammate packs)

The four teammate packs (`pr_review`, `pr_rework`, `story_development`,
`bug_development`) carry their own launch contract inside the release zip
(owner decision 2026-10-01):

| Zip entry | Content | Consumers |
|---|---|---|
| `launch.json` | verbatim copy of the root entry config (`pr_review.json`, …) | the factory's parent-config selection (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) |
| `loop/verdict.sh` | verbatim copy of `setup/review-verdict.sh` | the review-verdict step (pack wins, tree copy is the fallback) — review packs only |

`install.sh` / `cache.sh` deliberately stay in the dmtools-agents tree:
they install toolchain dependencies, they do not describe the agent. The
unpack cache lives at `~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/` (populated by
`dmtools run` resolving a `<agent>@latest` parent), so on fresh hosted
runners the legacy `factory-agents/<agent>.json` tree copy serves until
the pack is unpacked. Config-path audit: every tree reference in the four
launch configs (`descriptionPath`, `cliCommands`, JS actions, prompts)
already resolves INSIDE the zip — the compiler embeds the referenced
files and the runtime resolver rewrites the paths to the pack root.

### Patching rules — `smRuleOverrides`

Rules carry stable ids (`rework-on-red-ci`, `review-after-dev`,
`silent-update-behind`). Patch any field or disable a rule entirely:

```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    'validate-armed':       { limit: 2 },     // validate two PRs per tick
    'rework-on-red-ci':     { enabled: false } // manual rework only
  }
};
```

Jira-style rules still match by `configFile` key.

### PR lifecycle rules (#687) — test once per state

The merge loop is PR-carried (issue labels stay the dev→review contract):
`silent-update-behind` (ANY behind open non-draft PR → silent `github.token`
refresh, no CI — free freshness, the retired auto-update-prs workflow's
replacement; validating PRs excluded so their head never moves mid-run),
`validate-armed` (merge window: PAT update fires validation CI on the
final head + `ai_validating` marker), `fail-validation` (red → unarm,
report, re-arm `agent:rework` on the linked issue), `merge-validated`
(green + CLEAN → squash-merge, markers cleared). Note `labels` in SM
queries are **OR**-matched — the validating rules key on `ai_validating`
